label: FY27 Q2 (Jul–Sep 2026)
asOf: close of $174.62 on 6 Nov 2026; $191.80 before the report (4 Nov)
headline: License revenue up 50% but royalties up only 8%: data center doubled, phones were held back by memory prices, and next quarter's royalties grow only low single digits

points.t: Royalties rose 8%, below last quarter's guide of about 13%, and fell q/q from $715M to $670M. Data-center royalties doubled, but phone chips (over 40% of FY26 royalties) were held back by memory prices. Next quarter is guided to only low-single-digit growth.
License and other revenue rose 50% to $773M, mostly on the timing of several large deals. Annualized contract value grew only 12%, so part of it is pulled forward and won't repeat every quarter.

points.b: More confidence in its own chip
points.t: Arm AGI CPU orders run into 2027, with first deliveries in Jan–Mar 2027; the company is “more confident” in up to $2B of FY27–28 revenue, but none has been recognized yet.

reaction: Stock: closed at $166.72 the next day (5 Nov), down 13.1%; that day the Nasdaq fell about 4.5% and SMH 11.2% as the AI sector sold off on fears that data-center construction could be halted after the Democratic sweep. The royalty guide added stock-specific pressure. It rebounded to $174.62 on 6 Nov. Consensus via Finviz: revenue $1.38B, EPS $0.47; next quarter $1.53B, $0.55.

segments.title: Where the money comes from and goes
segments.bridgeT: From revenue to non-GAAP operating profit
segments.take: Arm has almost no production cost (98% gross margin); of every $1 of revenue about 56 cents goes to costs, R&D and sales/admin, leaving about 44 cents of operating profit. R&D is the biggest investment.

rows.why: Fees customers pay for new architectures (Armv9, compute subsystems CSS). Large-deal timing makes quarters swing: last quarter was only $574M. ACV (signed contracts annualized) grew only 12%, much steadier than revenue.

Paid on customer shipments: the rate per chip is rising (v9, CSS), data center doubled and physical AI such as cars grew 50%; but phones were held back by memory prices, and total royalties are guided to low-single-digit growth next quarter.

segments.note: The company doesn't disclose royalties by end market; “data center doubled” and “physical AI +50%” are from the shareholder letter. Shares are of this quarter's revenue.

extras.title: Where it sits in the AI loop
extras.take: Arm sells CPU designs and the instruction set. The cloud companies' own CPUs (AWS Graviton, Google Axion, Microsoft Cobalt) and NVIDIA's Grace/Vera are all Arm-based, so more AI data centers mean more royalties.

items.w: The company says Arm's share of server CPUs at the top hyperscalers rose from 15% in 2024 to over 50% in 2025, and expects over 60% by end-2026. AWS says Graviton revenue commitments grew more than 20x y/y.
AI agents call tools and run software, so CPUs do more work than in plain chat. NVIDIA's Vera CPU runs in production at OpenAI and is available on Oracle Cloud.
Arm AGI CPU is sold directly to cloud companies, competing with licensees that build CPUs on Arm (including Qualcomm and NVIDIA), which could strain licensing relationships over time.

AI data centers are absorbing memory capacity, and higher memory prices are squeezing phone shipments; Qualcomm's handset chip revenue fell 26% in the September quarter. Phone chips were over 40% of Arm's FY26 royalties.

extras.title: Where growth comes from
extras.take: Arm grows by charging more per chip (rates) plus data-center shipments, with a brand-new chip business on top. The real variables are when phones recover and whether the AGI CPU ships on time.

items.w: Partners shipped over 10 billion chips in a quarter for the first time, 1.5 billion more than a year ago. But unit growth is mostly in cheap chips; the money comes from data center and premium phones.
Armv9 and CSS carry higher royalty rates than older architectures. Licensing up 50% is a leading indicator for royalties: new designs reach volume two to three years later.
Up to $2B of revenue over FY27–28, with orders into 2027 and Oracle Cloud planning instances in 2027. Its own silicon will carry gross margins far below the 98% of licensing and royalties.
Only next-quarter guidance, with no annual or long-term revenue target. At the IPO it pointed to a long-term operating margin above 50%.
Phone royalties falling further; a licensing dispute with a big customer (Qualcomm); AGI CPU delays or a lack of TSMC capacity; policy slowing data-center construction.

trends.why: Five quarters in a row above 20% y/y, with licensing timing moving quarters around
Down q/q for two quarters as the phone drag shows

valuation.take: About 87 times trailing non-GAAP earnings and about 78 times FY27 consensus ($2.23), with a P/S of about 34. The price rests on the data-center and AGI CPU future; today's profits explain only a small part.

forward.title: FY27 (Apr 2026–Mar 2027) EPS
steps: Q4 backed out of consensus at about $0.70 → full year about $2.23
forward.note: The company gives no Q4 guidance. Consensus has Q4 well above Q3, partly from first AGI CPU deliveries and licensing seasonality.

scenarios.title: Three scenarios: FY29 (Apr 2028–Mar 2029) profits
head: Case
FY29 revenue
Operating margin
EPS
P/E at price
scenarios.note: Bear: phone royalties don't recover for two years and the AGI CPU ships only a fraction, about 13% a year; base: data-center royalties keep doubling and the AGI CPU adds about $1.5B a year, about 32% a year; bull: royalties and the AGI CPU both beat. EPS = revenue × non-GAAP operating margin × (1 − 16% tax) ÷ 1.08B shares. These assumptions are ours and are not forecasts.

pricezone.sub: FY29 EPS × our P/E; price at the 6 Nov close
pricezone.why: The price is above the zone and near the base case: buying at $175, the base case gains about 3% and the bear case loses about 41%, a reward/risk of about 0.1. At the $150 top of the zone it is about 0.6, at the $135 midpoint about 1.4, and at the $120 low end about 3.5. Our multiples sit below Arm's roughly 85x three-year average forward P/E: its own chips will pull margins down, so we don't think it should keep a pure-licensing multiple.

history.title: Against its own past
history.sub: P/S (TTM revenue, diluted shares), quarter ends; listed in September 2023, so 11 quarter ends from 2024Q1
history.note: About 34x now, below the post-IPO median of about 41x and less than half the 74x of end-June 2026. Quarterly revenue is from each shareholder letter, shares from SEC XBRL, quarter-end closes from Nasdaq.

cash.title: Non-GAAP EPS
cash.note: Operating cash flow was only $207M, mainly because contract assets rose $203M (license fees recognized but not yet billed) and other liabilities fell. Stock compensation of $376M, 26% of revenue, is the main reason GAAP profit is far below non-GAAP. Arm pays no dividend and buys back no stock; cash goes mainly to chip-business capacity and acquisitions.

valuation.next: Next shareholder letter around early February 2027.

changes.now: Actual +8% this quarter; next quarter guided to only low single digits, blamed on memory prices squeezing phones.

changes.before: Up to $2B of AGI CPU revenue over FY27–28, with supply the main risk.
changes.now: “Confidence increased over the last 90 days”: more supply, a better customer mix, orders into 2027.

changes.before: Disclosed remaining performance obligations (RPO) and the number of active licenses.
changes.now: No longer disclosed from FY27 Q1, because the chip business makes them “less relevant”.

insider.title: Insider trades
insider.text: Arm is a foreign private issuer, so its directors and officers don't file Form 4 and Insider Flow has no insider trades for it. Controlling shareholder SoftBank owns about 90%; any SoftBank buying or selling would show up in 13D/13G filings or UK RNS announcements.
